lines.spoken: Minimum capabilities of a good EDR:

lines.text: 2. Cisco Secure Endpoint
lines.spoken: 2. Cisco Secure Endpoint.

lines.text: Cloud-Based Architecture
lines.spoken: Cloud-Based Architecture.

lines.text: Gives endpoint visibility into files plus cloud-based malware detection, and the cloud keeps updating itself.
lines.spoken: Gives endpoint visibility into files plus cloud-based malware detection, and the cloud keeps updating itself.

lines.text: Known malware is detected fast because cloud resources do the work instead of endpoint resources, so the connector stays lightweight.
lines.spoken: Known malware is detected fast because cloud resources do the work instead of endpoint resources, so the connector stays lightweight.

lines.text: Cloud storage and processing give detailed reporting and strong management.
lines.spoken: Cloud storage and processing give detailed reporting and strong management.

lines.text: Runs on Windows, Mac, Linux, and Android endpoints.
lines.spoken: Runs on Windows, Mac, Linux, and Android endpoints.

lines.text: Unlike traditional antivirus with a local signature database, the connector sends a hash to the cloud and the cloud decides.
lines.spoken: Unlike traditional antivirus with a local signature database, the connector sends a hash to the cloud and the cloud decides.

lines.text: Figure 11-1: the endpoint sends SHA-256, Spero, and Ethos data to Talos and the Malware Analytics Cloud, which returns Clean, Malware, or Unknown.
lines.spoken: Figure 11 1: the endpoint sends SHA 256, Spero, and Ethos data to Talos and the Malware Analytics Cloud, which returns Clean, Malware, or Unknown.

lines.text: The connector can also act on its own, for example blocking malicious network connections using custom IP blacklists or dynamic lists of malicious IPs.
lines.spoken: The connector can also act on its own, for example blocking malicious network connections using custom IP blacklists or dynamic lists of malicious I.P.s.

lines.text: Connectors must reach the cloud, so they may need to pass through firewalls and web proxies.
lines.spoken: Connectors must reach the cloud, so they may need to pass through firewalls and web proxies.

lines.text: The book often calls the Secure Endpoint management console the "Malware Analytics Cloud console" and elsewhere the "Cisco Secure Endpoint console". Not in the book: Cisco Secure Malware Analytics (formerly Threat Grid) is the separate sandboxing product, so treat both names here as the Secure Endpoint console.
lines.spoken: The book often calls the Secure Endpoint management console the "Malware Analytics Cloud console" and elsewhere the "Cisco Secure Endpoint console". Not in the book: Cisco Secure Malware Analytics (formerly Threat Grid) is the separate sandboxing product, so treat both names here as the Secure Endpoint console.

lines.spoken: Web content filtering and redirect is not a Secure Endpoint feature (quiz question 1).

lines.text: Outbreak Control and Custom Detections
lines.spoken: Outbreak Control and Custom Detections.

lines.text: Start with Outbreak Control, because its objects are key parts of endpoint policies.
lines.spoken: Start with Outbreak Control, because its objects are key parts of endpoint policies.

lines.text: When you define a custom detection, endpoints quarantine matching files when they see them, and retrospection handles files seen before the detection existed.
lines.spoken: When you define a custom detection, endpoints quarantine matching files when they see them, and retrospection handles files seen before the detection existed.

lines.text: Simple custom detection steps:
lines.spoken: Simple custom detection steps:

lines.text: 1. Go to Outbreak Control > Custom Detections > Simple to see the existing list.
lines.spoken: 1. Go to Outbreak Control > Custom Detections > Simple to see the existing list.

lines.text: 2. Type a name in the Update Name box and click Save. The detection is added and opens for editing on the right side.
lines.spoken: 2. Type a name in the Update Name box and click Save. The detection is added and opens for editing on the right side.

lines.text: 3. Paste a SHA-256 hash and add a note, then click Save. Or upload a file, add a note, and click Upload; the hash appears at the bottom right.
lines.spoken: 3. Paste a SHA 256 hash and add a note, then click Save. Or upload a file, add a note, and click Upload; the hash appears at the bottom right.

lines.text: 4. Click Save, or the hash isn't stored.
lines.spoken: 4. Click Save, or the hash isn't stored.

lines.text: More simple detection options:
lines.spoken: More simple detection options:

lines.text: Upload a file of up to 20MB and the system pulls out its SHA-256.
lines.spoken: Upload a file of up to 20 megabytes and the system pulls out its SHA 256.

lines.text: Upload many hashes at once in a text file with one SHA-256 per line.
lines.spoken: Upload many hashes at once in a text file with one SHA 256 per line.

lines.text: The book describes these options right after the sentence introducing advanced detections, but they belong to simple detections, which use only SHA-256 hashes.
lines.spoken: The book describes these options right after the sentence introducing advanced detections, but they belong to simple detections, which use only SHA 256 hashes.

lines.text: Advanced custom detection steps:
lines.spoken: Advanced custom detection steps:

lines.text: 1. Go to Outbreak Control > Custom Detections > Advanced.
lines.spoken: 1. Go to Outbreak Control > Custom Detections > Advanced.

lines.text: 2. Type a name in the Name box and click Save.
lines.spoken: 2. Type a name in the Name box and click Save.

lines.text: 3. Click Edit to show the object's contents on the right side.
lines.spoken: 3. Click Edit to show the object's contents on the right side.

lines.text: 4. Add signatures. The signature type can be auto-detected or picked from the drop-down list (Figure 11-6).
lines.spoken: 4. Add signatures. The signature type can be auto-detected or picked from the drop-down list (Figure 11 6).

lines.text: 5. Click Build Database From Signature Set. A success message confirms the signature set was created.
lines.spoken: 5. Click Build Database From Signature Set. A success message confirms the signature set was created.

lines.text: Advanced signature types include file body-based signatures, MD5 signatures, and logical signatures (quiz question 4).
lines.spoken: Advanced signature types include file body-based signatures, M.D. 5 signatures, and logical signatures (quiz question 4).

lines.text: Every simple and advanced custom detection has a View Changes link to its audit log.
lines.spoken: Every simple and advanced custom detection has a View Changes link to its audit log.

lines.spoken: Android Custom Detections.

lines.text: Built by uploading the app's .apk file or picking it from the console's inventory list.
lines.spoken: Built by uploading the app's A.P.K. file or picking it from the console's inventory list.

lines.text: Outbreak control use: stops malware spreading through mobile devices. The user is notified and prompted to uninstall the malicious app.
lines.spoken: Outbreak control use: stops malware spreading through mobile devices. The user is notified and prompted to uninstall the malicious app.

lines.text: Application control use: stops apps you don't want installed. The user is notified and prompted to uninstall, just like with a malicious app.
lines.spoken: Application control use: stops apps you don't want installed. The user is notified and prompted to uninstall, just like with a malicious app.

lines.text: IP Blacklists and Whitelists
lines.spoken: IP Blacklists and Whitelists.

lines.text: Policies set what the connector does when DFC finds a suspicious connection, and which address sources DFC uses.
lines.spoken: Policies set what the connector does when DFC finds a suspicious connection, and which address sources DFC uses.

lines.text: Creating a list:
lines.spoken: Creating a list:

lines.text: 1. Go to Outbreak Control > Network > IP Block & Allow Lists and click Create IP List.
lines.spoken: 1. Go to Outbreak Control > Network > IP Block and Allow Lists and click Create IP List.

lines.text: 2. Name the list and choose IP Allow List (whitelist) or IP Block List (blacklist).
lines.spoken: 2. Name the list and choose IP Allow List (whitelist) or IP Block List (blacklist).

lines.text: 3. Type IPv4 addresses one per line, each line a single IP or CIDR, or upload a file of IPs. You can also specify port numbers to block or allow.
lines.spoken: 3. Type I.P. version 4 addresses one per line, each line a single IP or cider, or upload a file of I.P.s. You can also specify port numbers to block or allow.

lines.text: 4. Click Create IP List.
lines.spoken: 4. Click Create IP List.

lines.text: Changing a list: the book first says you edit it by downloading the file and uploading it back, then gives the fuller steps: click Download, delete the list, create a new list with the same name, and upload the modified file.
lines.spoken: Changing a list: the book first says you edit it by downloading the file and uploading it back, then gives the fuller steps: click Download, delete the list, create a new list with the same name, and upload the modified file.

lines.text: View Changes shows the IP list audit trail.
lines.spoken: View Changes shows the IP list audit trail.

lines.text: Application Control
lines.spoken: Application Control.

lines.text: Applications can be detected, blocked, and whitelisted, by SHA-256 hash, not by name.
lines.spoken: Applications can be detected, blocked, and whitelisted, by SHA 256 hash, not by name.

lines.text: Steps:
lines.spoken: Steps:

lines.text: 1. Go to Outbreak Control > Application Control > Blocked Applications and click Create.
lines.spoken: 1. Go to Outbreak Control > Application Control > Blocked Applications and click Create.

lines.text: 2. Name the list and click Save. You can't add apps before saving.
lines.spoken: 2. Name the list and click Save. You can't add apps before saving.

lines.text: 3. Click Edit, then add a SHA-256 hash, upload one application at a time (20MB limit) for the console to hash, or upload an existing list.
lines.spoken: 3. Click Edit, then add a SHA 256 hash, upload one application at a time (20 megabytes limit) for the console to hash, or upload an existing list.

lines.text: Exclusion Sets
lines.spoken: Exclusion Sets.

lines.text: Create one before building policies.
lines.spoken: Create one before building policies.

lines.text: Uses: resolve conflicts with other security products, and fix performance by excluding directories with large, frequently written files like databases.
lines.spoken: Uses: resolve conflicts with other security products, and fix performance by excluding directories with large, frequently written files like databases.

lines.text: If another antivirus product runs on the computer, exclude its install location.
lines.spoken: If another antivirus product runs on the computer, exclude its install location.

lines.text: Files in an excluded location are not checked by application blocking, simple custom detections, or advanced custom detections.
lines.spoken: Files in an excluded location are not checked by application blocking, simple custom detections, or advanced custom detections.

lines.text: Exclusion types:
lines.spoken: Exclusion types:

lines.text: Threat: by threat name.
lines.spoken: Threat: by threat name.

lines.text: Extension: by file extension.
lines.spoken: Extension: by file extension.

lines.text: Wildcard: wildcards in filenames, extensions, or paths.
lines.spoken: Wildcard: wildcards in filenames, extensions, or paths.

lines.text: Path: files in a given path. Windows paths can use CSIDL names.
lines.spoken: Path: files in a given path. Windows paths can use C.S.I.D.L. names.

lines.spoken: When one is updated, every policy using it updates too, and the change is pushed to connectors.

lines.spoken: Each row shows the operating system, set name, number of exclusions, number of groups using it, and number of computers using it.

lines.text: Search exclusion sets by name, path, extension, threat name, or SHA-256, and filter by operating system with the tabs.

lines.text: New set: Management > Exclusions, click New Exclusion Set, choose Windows, Mac, or Linux. The book's example uses macOS.
lines.spoken: New set: Management > Exclusions, click New Exclusion Set, choose Windows, Mac, or Linux. The book's example uses mac O.S.

lines.spoken: Click a set to expand its details.
